idiom_name: AsyncThrowingStream<[Page], Error> over URLSession async data(for:)
implementation_notes: Swift has no pagination type; the idiom is to model the endpoint as an AsyncThrowingStream (or any AsyncSequence) whose closure loops URLSession.shared.data(for:), decodes a Codable page carrying items and nextPageToken, yields the items and calls finish() when the token is nil, so callers use for try await with structured-concurrency cancellation. The classical manual form - a class holding the token plus nested completion handlers - survives only for pre-async/await deployment targets.
pitfalls: Cancellation must be wired through onTermination (or the task handle): otherwise a consumer that stops iterating leaves the page loop running and holding the connection.
An error after some pages were yielded must finish(throwing:), not be swallowed - and an unbounded continuation buffers pages if the producer outpaces the consumer.
